disease_label_per_paper: Listeria monocytogenes as a cause of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in alcoholic cirrhosis
presentation_summary: 74-year-old woman with alcoholic chronic liver disease, portal hypertension, esophageal varices, and prior upper digestive hemorrhage presented with one week of diffuse abdominal pain and increased abdominal perimeter.
On exam she had temperature 37.8 C, no remarkable blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, or oxygen saturation changes, marked abdominal distension, and a positive fluid wave.
Blood analysis showed hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, platelets 371,000/uL, WBC 16,090/uL, CRP 21.74 mg/dL, albumin 2.8 g/dL, and INR 1.52.
Ultrasound showed large-volume ascites; initial diagnostic/therapeutic paracentesis showed peritoneal fluid 3,136 leukocytes/mm3 with 86% neutrophils.
Listeria monocytogenes peritoneal-fluid culture, later CT exclusion of secondary peritonitis, antibiotic switch to ampicillin, and response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
